info.desc: Queens of the Stone Age is the self-titled debut album from Queens of the Stone Age. The album was released on September 22nd 1998 through Loosegroove Records, operated by Pearl Jam guitarist Stone Gossard, in the United States and Roadrunner Records in Europe. The vinyl version was released in three limited editions on Frank Kozik's record label Man's Ruin Records. In 2011, a remastered version was released under Josh Homme's own label, Rekords Rekords. This remaster went on to be reissued in 2024 by Matador Records, who also reissued the 1998 version on vinyl in 2022. The album features a .

podcast.body: Released in October 1998, this was an indie affair where Josh Homme played most of the instruments, with Fredo Hernandez on drums and a couple of friends filling in other parts. The album's final track, "I Was a Teenage Hand Model," famously concludes with a phone message of Nick Oliveri agreeing to join the band, signifying its intent to form a full lineup. "It was a self-titled indie affair."
